defects.description: The allowlist test compares a hostname with each listed host by suffix alone, so any third-party name that ends with a listed host (notexample-cdn.com for example-cdn.com) is admitted although the README admits only the listed hosts and their subdomains.

trigger.expected: D1 Allowlist({hosts:['example-cdn.com']}).check('https://notexample-cdn.com/track.gif') -> blocked egress blocked: host notexample-cdn.com is not on the allowlist

defects.why_missed: The suite admits a listed host and one of its subdomains, which the bare suffix test handles, and refuses a host with a different name entirely; the lookalike that satisfies the suffix while being a third party never appears.

defects.description: The internal-address rules are anchored at the scheme and tested against the raw URL string instead of the parsed hostname, so a URL whose text does not begin with an internal address reaches one: userinfo puts text in front of the real host and a numeric IPv4 form spells the same address another way.

trigger.expected: D2 Allowlist().check('https://example-cdn.com@127.0.0.1:8080/admin') -> blocked egress blocked: host 127.0.0.1 is an internal address

defects.why_missed: Every internal address the tests refuse is written at the front of the URL in its dotted form, which is exactly the shape the raw-string rules match, so the rules look like they check the address the request reaches.
